description: We are Kin Tech Titans, a student team from Kerala, India. We compete in WRO Future Innovators 2026 and have built real projects: AquaPatrol, a well-inspection drone with gas sensors, a fingerprint attendance system, and web apps using Firebase. For Space Apps we are building a game for the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge, using real NASA data. We are looking for teammates who know game design, JavaScript, UI/art design, or space science. Beginners are welcome!
summary: Mars Outpost: 10 Sols is a 3D survival game where students run a Mars base and must keep their crew alive for 10 sols. Players balance the same trade-offs a real crew faces: power from dusty solar panels, oxygen from a MOXIE-style O2 plant, food from a greenhouse with real space crops, and radiation shielding during solar storms. Every machine uses battery power, so turning one on means another may fail at night. Players clean the solar panels, replace filters, farm, store food, eat, exercise, sleep, use the airlock and spacesuit, and drive a rover on photo missions to collect rock samples and send science data to Earth. Solar storms based on Curiosity's real radiation data from May 2024 force the crew into a shelter, and a dust storm like the one that ended Opportunity cuts their power. Young learners feel every decision: if they plan badly, oxygen or food runs out and the mission fails. This makes real NASA engineering trade-offs tangible and fun.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Mars Outpost: 10 Sols is a 3D game where the player is an astronaut who must keep a Mars base alive for 10 sols (1 sol = 2 minutes, with day, night and a blue Mars sunset), followed by an endless bonus mode.

- Resources: oxygen, food, battery and radiation shield. The O2 plant, greenhouse and shield builder all use power. Solar panels give power only in daylight and lose power when they get dusty, so the player must choose which machines to keep on.

- Life in the base: an airlock where only one door may be open at a time, a spacesuit that must be worn outside, a fridge, meals at the table, an exercise bike and a bed to sleep and skip to the next sol.

- Farming: tomatoes plus 5 crops NASA has really grown (lettuce, radish, potato, dwarf wheat, chili pepper). Harvest -> food box -> fridge -> meal.

- Rover: drive with W/A/S/D on 3 photo missions (layered rocks, a dust devil, an iron meteorite), collect 8 mineral samples, analyse them in the lab and send the data to Earth with a realistic 3-22 minute radio delay.

- Danger: solar storms on sol 4 and sol 8 force the crew into a storm shelter, and a dust storm on sol 6 cuts solar power. If oxygen or food runs out, or the radiation dose gets too high, the mission fails (press R to restart).

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Students do not just read about Mars - they make the same trade-offs a real crew makes, and they see the results right away. Every event shows a short real NASA fact (press N to see all of them). The aim is to make young learners curious about space engineering and science.

CREATIVITY

A full 3D walkable outpost instead of a menu game, a science-based Mars walking gait (low gravity), real crops, real storm data and rover photo missions.

TOOLS

Godot 4.7.2 game engine, GDScript, Python (to generate the 3D models as glTF), Netlify for web hosting, and Claude (AI). It runs in a PC web browser with a keyboard and mouse.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Scientific accuracy, keeping it simple enough for young students, clear on-screen help (press H), and making it playable in a browser with no install.
